newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - KNP BT Q1 NET UP, SEES IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - KNP BT Q1 NET UP, SEES IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Dutch paper and office equipment group NV Koninklijke KNP BT surprised financial markets on Friday by announcing a first-quarter net profit rise of two million guilders to 52 million guilders.

"KNP BT reiterates its earlier forecast that the group's profit, assuming that the paper market does not slow down, will show a substantial improvement in the current year compared to 1996," the group forecast.
Analysts had expected KNP BT to post a first-quarter profit of 40-48 million guilders. Barely a month ago it said it expected lower first-quarter earnings.
But results were lifted by improvements in its flexible packaging activities and by majority-owned unit Gelderse Papier, which managed to climb out of the red.

KNP BT's protective and flexible packaging unit has recently been sold to Tenneco for $375 million, which will result in an one-off gain in the second quarter. Chief financial officer Rob Bonnier told Reuters Financial Television that the Tenneco deal was the major part of a strategy to focus on core activities.
He said no further major asset sales were planned in the short term.

Part of the one-off profit on the sale to Tenneco will be offset by restructuring charges. Bonnier said that previously announced job cuts in the Netherlands, Belgium and Austria were expected to start in the second half of this year.
Analysts welcomed the small first-quarter profit rise but added they were cautious on the outlook for the full year.
"If you look at those prospects, I think there is a fairly large uncertainty," Bank Bangert Pontier's Henk Brouwer said.

Analyst Jan Wirken of IRIS Research noted that KNP BT's higher first-quarter net, relatively soon after its warning that profits would fall, had proved once again that the company had difficulties in predicting its own results.
"Apparently the company still is not able to give a reliable forecast," Wirken said.

Brouwer said that if KNP BT's paper division could show a small positive result this year and its distribution and packaging sectors remained more or less steady, that alone would bring in a reasonable overall profit improvement.
Wirken also expected better results from the paper division.
"Not so much because business is doing well but more because it went so badly last year," he said.
First-quarter turnover increased to 3.71 billion guilders from a previous 3.41 billion, while net earnings per share rose to 0.42 guilders from 0.40.
Although KNP BT stock added one guilder to 39.40 in Amsterdam trading, analysts remained unconvinced that the shares were attractive.
"Given the uncertainty for the rest of the year, I think a higher share price today would be a good opportunity to say goodbye to the stock," Bangert's Brouwer said.
